solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Posed with your small goats

parts.note: to pose for a portrait is to sit, past tense sat
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone poses for a picture alongside your little goats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goats' is not livestock here but the figurative sense: lecherous men.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are slang for lustful, lecherous men, after the goat-legged woodland creatures of myth.

clue.text: Putting aside verse in broken English

indicators.note: in places the verse letter inside the rearranged letters
broken means smashed, so the letters of English are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A writer drops a poem written in poor English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges ENGLISH into SHELING, and 'in' puts V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To shelve a plan is to postpone or set it aside, as a book is put away on a shelf.

clue.text: Half-cut pedestrian ogles unclothed figure

indicators.note: the word pedestrian is cut in half and its second half kept
unclothed means stripped, so the outer letters of ogles are removed

explanation.surface: A drunk walker leers at a naked body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but here cuts off the first half of 'pedestrian' leaving TRIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle is a three-sided geometric figure.

clue.text: Terrible noise from strange Manx cat

parts.note: rum is British informal for odd or strange

indicators.note: the Manx cat famously has no tail, so the cat word loses its last letter

parts.note: puss is a familiar word for a cat

explanation.surface: An odd tailless cat from the Isle of Man makes a dreadful racket.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy disturbance or uproar.

clue.text: Discontentedly expostulates about dead mushroom

indicators.note: dis-contented: emptied of its contents, so only the outside letters of the following word remain

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about
late means dead, as in the late king

explanation.surface: An unhappy person complains about a mushroom that has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discontentedly' looks like a mood but means the word 'expostulates' is stripped of its contents, leaving ES. 'mushroom' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is to grow or spread rapidly, which is what something that escalates does.

clue.text: 14 in drunken stupor

indicators.note: drunken suggests staggering, so the letters of stupor are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lies in a drunken stupor.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 14 Across, a young growth on a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprout and a shoot are both new growth springing from a plant.

clue.text: Mad dictator imprisoning fanatic

indicators.note: the outer words hold the answer locked up inside them

explanation.surface: A crazed tyrant locks up an extremist.
explanation.definitionFit: An addict can mean an enthusiast or devotee, as in a jazz addict, so a fanatic.

clue.text: Missing most of sidereal year

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter

parts.note: sidereal and astral both mean relating to the stars

explanation.surface: Most of a star-measured year has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: A sidereal year is measured by the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Astray means gone off the right path, so lost or missing.

clue.text: Regularly defy arbiters in high places

indicators.note: regularly picks letters at a steady interval, here the even-placed ones of defy arbiters

explanation.surface: Someone habitually defies judges in positions of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high places' suggests people in authority but means the lofty nests of eagles.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyries are the nests of eagles and other birds of prey, built on cliffs and in tall trees.

clue.text: Beaming head off, boisterously closed book

indicators.note: boisterous means rowdy and unruly, so the remaining letters are thrown about into a new order
the head of the word Beaming is its first letter, which is cut off

explanation.surface: A beaming person loses their head and rowdily slams a book shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' removes the B from Beaming, leaving EAMING, and 'boisterously' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed book is an idiom for a person or thing that is a mystery, impossible to understand.

clue.text: Sci-fi villain parroted rubbish

indicators.note: as a verb rubbish means trash or wreck, so the letters of parroted are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A science-fiction baddie repeats nonsense like a parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Predator is the alien hunter of the 1987 film starring Arnold Schwarzenegger and its sequels.

clue.text: Very trendy old setters like wine

parts.note: in means fashionable
the setters of a puzzle speak of themselves as us

explanation.surface: Fashionable old crossword setters are said to be fond of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinous is an adjective meaning relating to or resembling wine, from Latin vinum.

clue.text: Indifferent gesture and silence over toupee

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means placed above, so the silence word comes first

parts.note: sh is the sound used to demand silence
rug is a humorous slang word for a toupee

explanation.surface: A wordless gesture of not caring about a hairpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrug is a raising of the shoulders showing indifference.

clue.text: Grip tea bag boxes

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so the bag word is wrapped around the tea word

parts.note: a purse is a small bag for money
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: An instruction to take hold of tea bag boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grip' is a noun, not a verb as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase means a firm hold or grip, as in failing to get purchase on a slippery slope.

clue.text: Need to evacuate Torquay after parking terminated

indicators.note: after means following, so the emptied word comes at the end

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
over means finished or ended

indicators.note: to evacuate a word is to empty it, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Torquay must be cleared once car parking has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: Torquay is an English seaside resort in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: Poverty is the state of being poor, so need or want.

clue.text: Go away and start to tighten belt

parts.note: shoo is what you say to drive someone off

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here the first letter of tighten

explanation.surface: Someone is told to leave and to pull in their belt a notch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belt' is a verb meaning to move very fast, not the strap around the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot and to belt are both informal verbs for rushing along at great speed.

clue.text: A duck, last to leave river

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so nil

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, here the end of leave

explanation.surface: A single duck is the final bird to leave the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great river of north-east Africa, flowing through Egypt.

clue.text: Prince leaves platform in disgust

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the prince's letter is taken out

parts.note: a podium is a raised platform for a speaker

explanation.surface: A royal storms off the stage in disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general hatred or contempt felt towards someone, close to disgust.

clue.text: Bits of blancmange perhaps hitting Dane

parts.note: blancmange is an example of a pud, British slang for pudding or dessert

indicators.note: hitting means battering, so the letters of Dane are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Pieces of a wobbly pudding strike a Danish man.
explanation.walkthrough: Blancmange is a set milk dessert. 'Bits' is used in its slang sense for the genitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Pudenda is a formal Latin word for the external genitals, which slang calls one's bits.

clue.text: According to Spooner, whimsical tosser is seasonal irritation

indicators.note: Rev William Spooner was famed for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: fey means whimsical or otherworldly
a heaver is one who heaves or throws, so a tosser

explanation.surface: A whimsical thrower is an annoyance at a certain time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: This allergy to pollen strikes in spring and summer, an irritation of the eyes and nose.

clue.text: Signal to wake First Lady, not so well after cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves the end letter round to the front

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in Genesis
iller means sicker, less well

explanation.surface: A US president's wife, unwell, signals to wake after a bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests a president's wife but is Eve. 'cycling' moves the last letter of EVEILLER to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Reveille is the bugle call or signal that rouses soldiers in the morning.

clue.text: Prudence and Carmen turning east

indicators.note: turning here means changing into something else, so one part of Carmen becomes another letter

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Two women, Prudence and Carmen, turn to face east.
explanation.walkthrough: Prudence looks like a woman's name but is the definition. 'turning' changes the MEN of Carmen into E.
explanation.definitionFit: Care and prudence both mean caution and attentiveness to avoid harm or risk.

clue.text: Little but combative Scotsman supports prohibition

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece supporting another sits beneath it

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
Tam is a Scottish man's name, short for Thomas

explanation.surface: A small but feisty Scot backs a prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantam is a small breed of chicken, hence a small but aggressive person, as in bantamweight.

clue.text: Sweetheart's first pet name for male sex organ

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, here of Sweetheart's

parts.note: a pet animal is tame

explanation.surface: A lover's first affectionate nickname for a private part.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds rude but is botanical.
explanation.definitionFit: The stamen is the pollen-producing male part of a flower.

clue.text: Thick skin of cold, retired Roman general

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the general's name runs backwards

parts.note: Sulla was a Roman general and dictator

explanation.surface: A tough skin belongs to an aloof retired Roman commander.
explanation.definitionFit: A callus is a hardened, thickened patch of skin.

clue.text: Good person ignoring the odds, robust and resolute

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for saint, a good person

indicators.note: skipping the odd-numbered letters of robust leaves its second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A virtuous person defies the odds, strong and determined.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout can mean brave and determined, as in a stout defence or stout-hearted.

clue.text: Mawkish drinker in empty speakeasy

indicators.note: in places the drinker inside the emptied word
an empty word has lost its inside, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: a lush is a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A sentimental drunk sits in a deserted illicit bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A speakeasy was an illegal bar in Prohibition-era America.
explanation.definitionFit: Slushy means sloppily sentimental, as mawkish does.

clue.text: Rebellious blighter ruthlessly guarding gun enclosure

indicators.note: rebellious suggests rising up or turning against, so the held letters run backwards
guarding means holding protectively, so the answer is held within the words

explanation.surface: A rebellious scoundrel ruthlessly defends a gun emplacement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guarding' holds TERRUT inside 'blighter ruthlessly', and 'Rebellious' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A turret is an armoured tower or housing on a tank or warship from which guns fire.

clue.text: Work with university pal, in fact

parts.note: to act is to function or work
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A student joins forces with a college friend, as it happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Actually and in fact are interchangeable adverbial phrases meaning really or as a matter of truth.

clue.text: Dull, obstinate person eating very loudly

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the stubborn person surrounds the musical letters

parts.note: a mule is a stubborn person, after the animal
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A dull, stubborn person chomps their food noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dull' is a verb, to deaden a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To muffle a noise is to deaden or dull it, as by wrapping something round a bell.

clue.text: Newspaper describing the French as "immutable"

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw around it, so the newspaper goes round the French article

parts.note: The Times is a British national newspaper
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: A newspaper calls the French people unchanging.
explanation.definitionFit: Something timeless is unaffected by passing time and so does not change.

clue.text: Labour leader getting behind campaign for tripe

indicators.note: getting behind means coming after, so the leader's letter follows the campaign word

parts.note: a drive is an organised campaign, as in a recruitment drive

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Labour

explanation.surface: The head of the Labour Party backs a political campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tripe' is not offal here but rubbish talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe and drivel are both informal words for nonsense or worthless talk.

clue.text: Is offended by articulate letter, in imagination

parts.note: to mind something is to object to or be upset by it

indicators.note: articulate means speak clearly, so the letter is pronounced, which gives a word sounding the same

parts.note: the letter here is I

explanation.surface: Someone is upset by a well-written letter, or so they imagine.
explanation.definitionFit: The mind's eye is the faculty of picturing things mentally, so imagination.

clue.text: Novelist partaking of lobster Newburg

indicators.note: partaking of means taking a share of, so the answer is part of the following words

explanation.surface: A writer is eating a lobster dish in a rich sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: Lobster Newburg is a dish of lobster in a sherry and cream sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was an eighteenth-century writer, author of Tristram Shandy.
